learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to express big, sudden emotions in your writing using fun exclamation words and punctuation!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An interjection is a short word or phrase thrown into a sentence to express a strong, sudden feeling! It has no real grammatical connection to the rest of the sentence, it is just pure emotion.
When you are super happy, excited, or want to praise someone, you use words like 'Hurrah!', 'Yay!', or 'Bravo!' For example: 'Hurrah! We won the cricket match!'
If something shocks you or looks beautiful, you might say 'Wow!' or 'Oh!' If you accidentally bump your toe, you use an interjection of pain like 'Ouch!' or 'Alas!'
Interjections almost always need a special punctuation mark to show that strong feeling! We put an exclamation mark (!) directly after the interjection.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Emotion Reaction Game
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you just saw a beautiful rainbow, then imagine you just dropped your favourite ice cream. Write down exactly what you would say using an interjection for both moments!

quick_recap: ⭐ Interjections are short words used to express sudden and strong feelings.
⭐ They can show joy (Hurrah!), surprise (Wow!), or pain (Ouch!).
⭐ An interjection is almost always followed by an exclamation mark (!).
